messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty: page fired for service=infra-infer-canary alert=deploy_canary_latency_surge severity=P1. Runbook: https://redwood-internal/runbooks/canary-latency. Pager: oncall-rotation -> please ack and triage.

oncall-rotation: acked. I’m on it — taking P1. pinging sre_jordan.

sre_jordan: I’m looking at metrics now. p95 up from 220ms -> 1.8s on canary, 5xx rate up ~3.2% (baseline 0.2%). Top traces point to tokenizer/convert stage in model pipeline, lots of repeated retries.

alex_p: noticed same in dashboards. Canary rollout id=rl-20260315-77 commit=ad9f4c2. Deployed ~12:30 UTC.

deploy-bot: rollout rl-20260315-77 -> canary fraction=10% -> images: inference:v20260315-ad9f4c2.

maria_ops: tagging potential customer impact: EU region saw elevated timeouts (5xx). Recommend divert traffic off canary and pause rollout while we triage.

sre_jordan: agree. Quick mitigation: pause rollout and divert new traffic to stable. I’ll run commands now.

sre_jordan: ```sh
# pause the canary rollout
kubectl -n inference rollout pause deployment/infer-serving-canary-rl-20260315-77
# scale canary down to 0 replicas (if pause isn't enough)
kubectl -n inference scale deploy/infer-serving-canary --replicas=0
# toggle traffic router (internal) to route canary -> stable
curl -X POST -H \"Authorization: Bearer $SECRET\" https://router.internal/route -d '{"service":"infer","target":"stable"}'
```

alex_p: going to open the router call to ops for confirmation: @maria_ops please confirm you see the router change once call returns.

maria_ops: seeing router change now, traffic fraction to stable ~100%. :white_check_mark:

sre_jordan: scaled canary to 0, pause confirmed. Error rate dropping on stable. p95 trending back to normal for stable, canary still glitchy.

oncall-rotation: PD note updated: ack by oncall-rotation at 1829009999, mitigations applied (traffic diversion + pause). Escalation suppressed.

cs_oliver: quick question from support — any known customer impact? we’ve got a ticket from ACME Corp reporting timeouts in EU around 12:40 UTC. Can we confirm whether they hit canary?

sre_jordan: initial logs show ~3% of traffic went to canary during ramp. ACME sessions show repeated tokenizer timeouts ~12:34-12:42 UTC, correlation matches. Likely root cause for their ticket.

alex_p: I'm drafting a short customer note to CS. Suggest wording: "We briefly rolled a canary that increased latency/timeouts for a small subset (~3%) of requests in EU; we've paused the rollout and rolled back canary to stable. We're investigating root cause and will follow up." @cs_oliver ok to send?

cs_oliver: ok please include ETA for follow-up and whether there was data loss (none observed). send now as interim.

sre_jordan: collecting heap/CPU profiles and tokenizer debug logs. Early hypothesis: a change in tokenizer config (commit ad9f4c2) caused pathological processing for some inputs (edge-case token sequences) leading to retries and increased CPU on the pipeline.

alex_p: can we reproduce locally? if tokenizer change, open PR to revert config or gate it behind flag. Also we should add rate-limit / circuit-breaker in tokenizer stage.

sre_jordan: spinning up a repro with a sampled failing input. If we can confirm, we'll either revert the commit or patch and cut a hotfix.

deploy-bot: rollout rl-20260315-77 marked PAUSED by sre_jordan.

maria_ops: will coordinate postmortem and communications. Action items I’m tracking: 1) customer interim note (cs_oliver) 2) revert/patch decision (eng) 3) adjust canary ramp policy (eng/sre) 4) update alert thresholds to avoid noisy pages (sre)

alex_p: I’ll open an incident ticket and assign to eng-runtime and eng-ml for root cause. provisional owner: eng-runtime lead (assigned).

oncall-rotation: marking incident as mitigated in PD at 1829011800 since traffic diverted and canary paused. leaving thread open until root cause confirmed.

cs_oliver: sent customer interim note at 12:58 UTC. They asked for postmortem when available.

sre_jordan: logs and profiles uploaded to the incident folder: https://redwood-internal/incidents/1829009999/artifacts. Early repro succeeds for some long-token sequences. Opening PR to revert tokenizer config in ad9f4c2 now.

alex_p: thanks. Suggested follow-up timeline: 3h confirm root cause & revert/patch, 24h postmortem. Also recommend decreasing canary ramp from 10% -> 2% and add circuit-breaker to tokenizer stage before next rollout.

maria_ops: agreed. I’ll coordinate the postmortem doc and schedule a 30-min blameless review with eng & SRE.

oncall-rotation: final note: PD incident closed (mitigated) 1829013600. Will reopen if regression reappears. Good triage everyone. :tada:
